title: Sparse parity on the ET-SoC-1
description: A noisy sparse parity solver for all 1,024 kernel minions of the ET-SoC-1: an exhaustive correlation search written as an int8 matrix product on the tensor units, checked on every run by two closed-form checksums over all the candidates and a CPU oracle. On aifoundry3's card it solves (512, 4, 0.4, 1,850), 2.83 billion candidates, in 0.323 s: 12× one core of the host's i7-11700K and 1.6× six tuned AVX-512 threads at the same risk of missing the secret. Across three sizes it is 7.8–12× one core, 1.1–1.6× six threads and about level with the whole 16-thread host (extrapolated). Measured on the one-stage scan, the board alone uses 2.5–7.7× less energy per solve than the CPU's assumed package energy (1.6–6.1× with the host that drives the card). Why these sizes, how the scan maps onto the chip, the five milestones, the energy, and where the time goes.
